newsitem.title: USA: CRP acreage cap unfair, unwise -- US farm group.
newsitem.headline: CRP acreage cap unfair, unwise -- US farm group.

text.p: Congress will be breaking faith with U.S. farmers if it approves a plan to limit new enrollment into the Conservation Reserve to 14 million acres this year, the American Farm Bureau Federation said Friday.
The proposal was adopted Wednesday by a House Appropriations subcommitte as part of a supplemental appropriations bill.
The full committee will examine the bill next week.

In a statement, AFBF president Dean Kleckner said it was unfair for lawmakers to meddle with enrollment, considering Congress reauthorized the reserve last year. An acreage cap will interfere with smooth operation of the program, he said.

"We can't let the appropriations process decide what land should be farmed and what needs to remain out of production," Kleckner said, arguing "it is premature to judge the outcome" of a sign-up held in March.

"With 22 million acres coming out of the (Conservation Reserve Program) this fall and another five million acres for which 10-year contracts are scheduled to expire next year, we need to be moving ahead with both the re-enrollment and new enrollment to help our farmers and their lenders plan for future use of their land."
AFBF said the cap was proposed by lawmakers who want to use CRP to protect water quality but whose home states showed low interest in this year's signup.
